```{python}
import qrcode
from pathlib import Path

Path("qr").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
for name, url in {
    "itables":      "https://github.com/mwouts/itables",
    "datatables":   "https://github.com/AllanJard",
    "jupytext":     "https://jupytext.org",
    "linkedin":     "https://linkedin.com/in/marc-wouts",
    "presentation": "https://mwouts.github.io/pydata_london_2026_itables_and_jupytext_lightning_talk/",
}.items():
    qr = qrcode.QRCode(border=2, error_correction=qrcode.constants.ERROR_CORRECT_L)
    qr.add_data(url)
    qr.make(fit=True)
    qr.make_image(fill_color="black", back_color="white").save(f"qr/{name}.png")
```

## When and How to use ITables

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="65%"}
- Tired of using `df.head()`?
- Want to see more rows and columns of `df`?
- Looking for interactivity?
:::

::: {.column width="35%"}
> ITables is just about *display*.
>
> Pandas and Polars calculations are unaffected.
:::

<br>

::::

````{=html}
<div class="jt-formats" id="it-formats">
  <div class="jt-tablist" role="tablist">
    <button class="jt-tab jt-active" onclick="itSwitch(0)">Notebook Mode</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="itSwitch(1)">Widget</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="itSwitch(2)">Streamlit</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="itSwitch(3)">Dash</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="itSwitch(4)">HTML</button>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel jt-active" id="it-0">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">notebook.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code>import itables

itables.init_notebook_mode()</code></pre>
    </div>
    <ul class="jt-note-list">
      <li>Works in JupyterLab, Notebook, Google Colab, VS Code, Quarto.</li>
      <li>Turns every <code>df</code> into an interactive datatable.</li>
      <li>Compatible with <code>nbconvert --to html</code>.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="it-1">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">notebook.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code>from itables.widget import ITable

ITable(df)</code></pre>
    </div>
    <p class="jt-note">Works in Jupyter, Marimo, Shiny and Panel.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="it-2">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">app.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code>from itables.streamlit import interactive_table

interactive_table(df)</code></pre>
    </div>
    <p class="jt-note">Drop-in for <code>st.dataframe</code> — full DataTables features in Streamlit.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="it-3">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">app.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code>from itables.dash import ITable

ITable(df)</code></pre>
    </div>
    <p class="jt-note">ITables component for Dash apps.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="it-4">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">report.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code>from itables import to_html_datatable

html = to_html_datatable(df)</code></pre>
    </div>
    <p class="jt-note">Export a standalone HTML file with a fully interactive table — no server required.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
function itSwitch(idx) {
  document.querySelectorAll('#it-formats .jt-tab').forEach(function(t, i) {
    t.classList.toggle('jt-active', i === idx);
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('#it-formats .jt-panel').forEach(function(p, i) {
    p.classList.toggle('jt-active', i === idx);
  });
}
</script>
````

## A Pandas DataFrame rendered with ITables

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column .side-notes width="20%"}
<br>

**By default**

- Paging
- Sorting
- Searching
- Horizontal scroll

**Advanced options**

- Caption
- CSV and Excel export
- Advanced filtering
- Fixed columns, etc
:::

::: {.column width="80%"}
```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML

display(HTML("<style>.dt-container { font-size: medium; }</style>"))

from itables.sample_dfs import get_countries
import itables
df = get_countries()
itables.show(df)
```
:::

## Jupytext

::: {.eyebrow}
Jupyter Notebooks become `.py` or `.md` files (and vice versa)
:::

With Jupytext installed, any of these files becomes a notebook in Jupyter 🪄 (right click, _open with notebook_)

````{=html}
<div class="jt-formats" id="jt-formats">
  <div class="jt-tablist" role="tablist">
    <button class="jt-tab jt-active" onclick="jtSwitch(0)">py:percent</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="jtSwitch(1)">py:light</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="jtSwitch(2)">py:marimo</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="jtSwitch(3)">Markdown</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="jtSwitch(4)">MyST</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="jtSwitch(5)">Quarto</button>
    <button class="jt-tab" onclick="jtSwitch(6)">Pandoc</button>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel jt-active" id="jt-0">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">notebook.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code># %% [markdown]
# # Analysis
# A quick look at the data.

# %%
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
df.describe()</code></pre>
    </div>
    <p class="jt-note">30+ languages supported. Works in VS Code, PyCharm, Spyder...</p>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="jt-1">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">notebook.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code># # Analysis
# A quick look at the data.

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
df.describe()</code></pre>
    </div>
    <p class="jt-note">Minimal cell markers</p>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="jt-2">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">notebook.py</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code>import marimo

__generated_with = "0.23.8"
app = marimo.App()


@app.cell
def _():
    import marimo as mo
    return (mo,)


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md(r"""
    # Analysis
    A quick look at the data.
    """)
    return


@app.cell
def _():
    import pandas as pd
    df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
    df.describe()
    return


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()</code></pre>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="jt-panel" id="jt-3">
    <div class="jt-card">
      <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">notebook.md</span></div>
      <pre class="jt-pre"><code># Analysis

A quick look at the data.

```python

```</code></pre>
````

## Paired notebooks

::: {.eyebrow}
Jupytext · one config line
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}
````{=html}
<div class="jt-card">
  <div class="jt-bar"><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-dot"></span><span class="jt-fname">jupytext.toml</span></div>
  <pre class="jt-pre"><code>formats = "ipynb,py:percent"</code></pre>
</div>
````
This pairs every `.ipynb` with a `.py` notebook. Both stay in sync — the `.ipynb` keeps the **outputs**, the `.py` holds the **inputs** and takes precedence.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Notebooks in **version control** — just clean `.py` diffs
- Edit with **any text editor**, IDE, or code review tool
- Text files are **1,000× smaller** than `.ipynb`

<br>

*And with AI, this becomes a game-changer.*
:::

::::
